[General] Phase 3 of the linked issue explicitly applies the 2.x compatibility and 3.0 removal policy, so saying this setter may disappear in the next minor release incorrectly permits removal during 2.x. Document the 3.0 timeline instead.

This issue also appears on line 95 of the same file.
threads.hunk:
@@ -44,27 +45,61 @@ public JettyClientTelemetryBuilder addAttributesExtractor( return this; } + /** + * Configures which HTTP request headers are captured as span attributes. + * + *

Selector patterns are matched case-insensitively, since HTTP header names are + * case-insensitive. {@code ?} matches one character and {@code *} matches any number of + * characters, including none. Excluded patterns take precedence over included patterns. A + * selector with no included patterns captures every header that is not excluded, and an + * {@linkplain IncludeExclude#isEmpty() empty} selector captures no headers. + */ + @CanIgnoreReturnValue + public JettyClientTelemetryBuilder setRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude requestHeaders) { + builder.setRequestHeaders(requestHeaders); + return this; + } + /** * Configures HTTP request headers to capture as span attributes. * * @param requestHeaders HTTP header names to capture. + * @deprecated Use {@link #setRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude)} instead. May be removed in the next + * minor release. */ + @Deprecated // may be removed in the next minor release

replies.body:
Keeping `may be removed in the next minor release` here. The removal timeline follows the stability of the publishing artifact rather than how the class looks, and this builder ships from an `-alpha` artifact: `instrumentation/jetty-httpclient/jetty-httpclient-9.2/library` has no `gradle.properties` at all, so it never sets `otel.stable=true`, while `instrumentation-api/gradle.properties` does.

`.github/agents/knowledge/api-deprecation-policy.md` addresses this case directly. It names `*TelemetryBuilder` in `instrumentation/**/library` as a class that looks like supported public API but is published only from `-alpha` artifacts, it says "Do not schedule an alpha-only deprecation for 3.0 — it does not have to wait for a major version", and it lists "`to be removed in 3.0` on an alpha-only symbol" as a review flag whose remedy is exactly this wording.

The 3.0 language in #19444 applies to the stable `instrumentation-api` extractor builders, `HttpClientAttributesExtractorBuilder` and `HttpServerAttributesExtractorBuilder`, whose deprecated setters do say "To be removed in 3.0". This PR only touches alpha library builders.

I did revise the tag for a different reason, to warn that the replacement matches glob patterns rather than literal header names, so anyone migrating a `"*"` value sees the behavior change at the point of migration.

threads.body: [General] This compatibility claim is not implemented: the deprecated request and response setters still call `DefaultHttpClientInstrumenterBuilder#setCaptured*Headers`, which builds an `IncludeExclude` selector. With the new header-name enumeration, `*` and `?` are therefore evaluated as globs; for example, `?` can capture any one-character header instead of a header literally named `?`. Route both deprecated setters through a true exact-name path to avoid unexpectedly capturing sensitive headers.
threads.hunk:
@@ -44,22 +45,66 @@ public JettyClientTelemetryBuilder addAttributesExtractor( return this; } + /** + * Configures which HTTP request headers are captured as span attributes. + * + *

Selector patterns are matched case-insensitively, since HTTP header names are + * case-insensitive. {@code ?} matches one character and {@code *} matches any number of + * characters, including none. Excluded patterns take precedence over included patterns. A + * selector with no included patterns captures every header that is not excluded, and an + * {@linkplain IncludeExclude#isEmpty() empty} selector captures no headers. + */ + @CanIgnoreReturnValue + public JettyClientTelemetryBuilder setRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude requestHeaders) { + builder.setRequestHeaders(requestHeaders); + return this; + } + /** * Configures HTTP request headers to capture as span attributes. * + *

The header names are matched literally. Unlike {@link #setRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude)}, + * {@code *} and {@code ?} are not treated as glob patterns, since this setting never documented + * them as wildcards.

replies.body:
I verified this rather than dismissing it, because a stale base and a genuine widening produce identical symptoms here.

You're right about what this branch does *in isolation*, and wrong about what merges. `DefaultHttpClientInstrumenterBuilder#setCapturedRequestHeaders` no longer converts to an `IncludeExclude`: base commit `1572a0077b` routes it through `CapturedHttpHeaders.createExact`, which stores the names as a literal set and never builds a selector. That commit is on the base branch `trask/http-header-selectors-api`, not in this PR's diff, so a review of the head branch alone reads the pre-fix version — which is exactly the globbing you quote, and exactly why `HttpHeadersTest.java:169` still shows the old expectation on this ref.

The measurement, using `deprecatedSettersMatchHeaderNamesLiterally` in `JettyHttpClient9HeaderSelectorTest`, which passes `"*"` through the deprecated setters and asserts nothing is captured:

- On head `ed305c31dc` alone: **fails**, with `http.request.header.accept-encoding` on the span. That is the widening you describe.
- On the merge ref `685943908c` (`git fetch origin refs/pull/19603/merge`, parents `1572a0077b` + `ed305c31dc`): **passes**, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`.

CI builds `refs/pull/N/merge`, so the green run is the one that reflects what would land. I'm deliberately not rebasing to make this visible to a head-only review; that would cost a force-push and clear the review check run without changing any merged behavior.

Resolving as a stale-base false positive, with the caveat that the regression test above is now permanent — if anyone reintroduces the selector conversion on either side, it fails loudly.
